name: Kraak porcelain
summary: Thin blue-and-white export porcelain from Jingdezhen. Plates and bowls have a rim in 8 panels that frame plants and sacred objects, and a central scene. Merchants of Portugal and the Netherlands sold it across Europe.

philosophy.core_thesis: One cobalt blue on a white porcelain body, ordered in panels that a quick painter can repeat, makes a pattern that a whole continent wants to buy.
design_principles: Divide the rim into 8 panels, in turn broad and narrow, and fill each with a plant, a jewel or a precious object.
Paint a single scene in the well: a bird on a rock, a deer, or a vase of flowers.
Paint the cobalt under the glaze with a loaded brush, and shade the blue with a pale wash.
Throw the porcelain very thin, with a wall 2 to 3 mm thick, so that it is light and translucent.
Use a clear glaze with a slight blue-grey tone and fire the dish in a wood-fired kiln.
Leave the edge of the rim with a thin brown iron line, where the glaze runs thin.
Pack the plates in stacks of 20 or more for the ship; a set is of one size and one pattern.
anti_patterns: A thick opaque white tin glaze on an earthenware body
A printed pattern with even hard lines
Red, green or gold enamel over the glaze
A deep, rich blue like the ware of the 18th century

form.shape: Wide dishes with a flat rim, rimmed bowls with a flared lip, small plates, and ewers and jars for export.
form.profile: A shallow well and a wide rim that is flat or slightly lobed; some bowls have a broad rim that folds out like a cap.
form.foot_and_rim: A narrow foot ring with a sandy, unglazed base and a brown rim line; the foot of a dish is often chipped, from the kiln sand.
form.proportion: Dish diameter 20 to 50 cm and wall 2 to 4 mm thick; the rim is about one third of the radius.
rules: Keep the rim flat and one third of the radius, so that the panels have room.
Fire the dishes on a bed of sand, and leave the sand marks on the foot.
Make the wall thin and light; the weight must be low for the ship.

bodies.rule: Use a white kaolin and petuntse porcelain that fires dense and translucent. Do not use earthenware: the whole value is the thin white body.

methods: turning the foot and the well when leather-hard
painting the cobalt on the raw body
stacking the dishes on sand in saggars
forming.joins: Spouts and handles of ewers are luted with slip; a lid fits on a rebated seat.
forming.details: Light sand marks on the foot, a thin brown line at the rim, and a small blue blur where the cobalt sank into the glaze.

glaze.pattern: Panels of Buddhist emblems, flowers and jewels on the rim; a deer, a bird, or a flower vase in the well.
glaze.gloss: Soft gloss, about 60 to 80 GU, with a faint blue-grey glaze.
glaze.wear: The glaze stays hard; the brown rim line and the sandy foot show the ship and the market.

palette.strategy: A grey-blue cobalt on a white, slightly cool ground, in two tones, with a brown line at the rim.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired kiln at Jingdezhen, with the dishes stacked in saggars.
processes: painting cobalt on the raw body
firing.scale: Thousands of pieces a year went to the Netherlands, Portugal and the colonies in Asia.
firing.signs: A sandy foot, a brown rim line, and a soft blue blur in the painted lines.

pieces.form: Large dish with an 8-panel rim and a deer in the well
Plate with a wide flat rim in 8 panels and a flower vase in the well
Rimmed bowl with a broad panelled lip, the cap bowl called klapmuts
Small plate with a bird on a rock and a thin incised line at the rim

positive: deer or bird in the well

canonical_works.work: Cargo of the carrack Santa Catarina, sold at Amsterdam

evidence.title: Porcelain dish from Jingdezhen, Wanli period

emotion.target_response: A cool, orderly wonder: the viewer sees a far-off world in blue on a fine white dish and wants to own a set.

use_cases: a pattern brief for a panelled blue-and-white plate
a Dutch Golden Age still-life prompt
a museum label on export porcelain
avoid_when: the brief needs a thick tin-glazed earthenware
the brief wants a European polychrome style
the brief wants a printed industrial pattern

modifiers.how: Change the body to buff earthenware with a thick white tin glaze, and keep the panelled rim and the cobalt.
Keep the porcelain body and add overglaze enamel and gold in a modelled European form.
Change the body to white earthenware and print the blue pattern from a copper plate.
